1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Serra Vale Growers' Cooperative (fictional) packs mandarins from about 140 member growers in three districts (Lower Serra, Upper Serra, Coastal Flats) and exports them to a single importer, Nordhafen Fresh Imports. This season it used two ocean carriers: Meridane Line (cheaper, transships at Port Calder) and Coastway Shipping (direct sailing). Several changes landed in late July and early August: a new postharvest fungicide supplier (Pellacor), storms over Lower Serra, a new packhouse night-shift supervisor, and a new export documentation suite (Tallis) for Meridane bookings.
9	Your request: Five of the nine containers shipped between 1 Aug and 5 Sep were rejected on arrival for mould decay above the contract tolerance. The importer has warned that one more rejection will trigger a review of the season's program. The general manager wants to suspend Lower Serra growers and claim against Meridane. The quality manager wants to go back to the old fungicide. The board asks what caused the rejections and what should be done before the next sailings.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Nordhafen Fresh Imports, arrival inspection summary (customer-account): Arrival inspection summary from Nordhafen Fresh Imports, sent 2 Oct. Contract tolerance: decay at arrival not above 3% of fruit. K1 (Meridane, sailed 1 Aug) 1.4%, accepted. K2 (Coastway, 4 Aug) 1.1%, accepted. K3 (Meridane, 8 Aug) 11.2%, REJECTED. K4 (Meridane, 15 Aug) 9.4%, REJECTED. K5 (Coastway, 18 Aug) 1.9%, accepted. K6 (Meridane, 22 Aug) 13.8%, REJECTED. K7 (Coastway, 29 Aug) 0.8%, accepted. K8 (Meridane, 29 Aug) 10.6%, REJECTED. K9 (Meridane, 5 Sep) 12.5%, REJECTED. Decay: green and blue mould. Pallet survey, rejected containers only: pallets with Lower Serra grower codes averaged 15.1% decay, other pallets 10.3%. Stowage positions not recorded. A further rejection will trigger a review of the season's program.
12	- Packhouse exit QC log, summary prepared by QA clerk (log): Packhouse exit QC log, summary for K1–K9. All nine containers: decay at packing-line exit 0.2–0.5% (spec: not above 1%). Pulp temperature at container loading 3.6–4.3°C for every container, against the cooperative's export carriage specification of 4°C. Postharvest fungicide: Pellacor (new supplier) delivered 2 Aug and in use from that date; the previous supplier's remaining drums were used alongside it until about 12 Aug. Per-container drum records are held in the packing system. Lower Serra deliveries usually arrived after 16:00 and were packed on the night shift throughout August. Night-shift supervisor changed on 3 Aug.
13	- Email, D. Achterberg (Quality Manager) to H. Voss (General Manager), 3 Oct (manager-account): 'Helena, the timing is hard to ignore. Procurement moved us to Pellacor to save 18% on fungicide, and the drums arrived on 2 August. K1 and K2 were packed before then and both passed. Since then we have lost five of seven. The Coastway containers that passed are on a direct sailing, so my reading is that the weaker product holds up on a short trip but not on Meridane's transshipment route. Green and blue mould is exactly what a failing fungicide looks like. I recommend we go back to the old supplier immediately, whatever it costs.'
14	- Memo, H. Voss (General Manager) to the board, 6 Oct (leadership-account): 'Two issues. First, Nordhafen's own pallet survey shows Lower Serra fruit is the worst in every failed container. Those growers picked straight after the late-July storms against our field officers' advice. I propose suspending Lower Serra deliveries for the rest of the season and withholding their August payments pending review. Second, every rejected container went on Meridane. Their reply that the units ran to our instructed setpoint is what any carrier would say. I have asked our broker to prepare a cargo claim for all five rejected containers on the basis of refrigeration failure.'
15	- Interview notes, P. Lemaire (logistics coordinator), 6 Oct (staff-account): Since 4 Aug, Meridane bookings go through the new Tallis export documentation suite, which submits shipping instructions to Meridane's portal electronically. 'It pulls the product details from the master file, so I don't retype anything.' Coastway is not connected yet; their bookings still go by email using the old spreadsheet template, with a move to Tallis planned for November. The implementation contractor, Brindle Systems, set up the master file in the week before go-live. Meridane routes via transshipment at Port Calder, usually 24–27 days; Coastway sails direct, usually 21–25 days. 'Meridane is cheaper, so we put more on them.'
16	- Letter, Meridane Line claims desk, 3 Oct (vendor-account): Reply to the cooperative's notice of rejection. 'We have reviewed the voyages for K3, K4, K6, K8 and K9. Our refrigerated units operated to the setpoint stated in your shipping instructions throughout carriage, and no equipment alarms were raised at sea or during transshipment. We do not accept liability for the condition of the cargo on arrival. Controller downloads can be provided on formal request through your broker.'
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The rejections trace to a data error in our own systems. When the Tallis product record for mandarins was created on 1 Aug, it was copied from the avocado record and kept avocado's 7.0°C carriage temperature. Our specification for mandarins is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container booked through Tallis (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was sent at 7.0°C and ran at 7.0°C, and every one was rejected. The 4.0°C containers (K1, K2, K5, K7) all passed, including those packed with Pellacor, so the new fungicide isn't the cause. Meridane's units held the setpoint we gave them, so a claim against them would fail. Lower Serra fruit made up 28–40% of every container, accepted ones included, so suspending those growers isn't justified. I'm about 90% sure of this. Next steps, in order: (1) Correct the mandarin record in Tallis today. (2) Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4.0°C. (3) Add a check that compares the reefer setting with the product specification before each submission. (4) Hold off on the cargo claim, the grower suspension and the Pellacor reversal. Independent loggers are a reasonable extra safeguard. Review the sign-off process, not individual blame.
20
